title: Design: the Location menu with two locations matches the design picture
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • Starting screen: A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu in light theme at 100% zoom.
  • The design picture "The native Location menu" (ar-ap-p4-the-native-location-menu.png) is attached to this case and open beside the browser at 100% zoom; compare the layout, labels and styles, not the names and amounts, which are only examples.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the Location chip.
  2. Widen the browser window to 1536 px and look across the page.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the menu opens under the chip; as in the picture, while the menu is open the chip shows a circled "×" in place of its down arrow; the menu rows read, top to bottom, "Select all" with "2 selected" at its right, {Location-A}, {Location-B}, a dividing line, then "Clear selection"; no search box; the ticked boxes have a light-blue fill with a blue tick.
  • Step 2: nothing overlaps, is cut off or clipped; the layout is the same as at 1440 px.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R2: “The Location chip and its open menu are the native ones, exactly as on Sales By Customer, Inventory Value and Work In Progress: label "Location" with the location pin icon; the menu shows a "Select all" row, a "{N} selected" count, the locations with the ticked ones first, a search box with the placeholder "Search locations" once there are more than 8 locations, and "Clear selection".”
  • S5-R5: “The filter opens with every location in the list ticked (All locations), so an untouched report shows exactly today's organization-wide rows and totals. "Select all" ticks every location again.”
  • S5-R4: “Each location is named exactly as the location switcher in the top right of ShopView names it, and the Location column uses the same name.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 4 "Location filter and Location column" (board Location.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p4-the-native-location-menu.png: figure "The native Location menu" (This build (after)), board "4. Location filter and Location column"

The design's own words:

  • ""Select all" with "2 selected", every location in this report's own data named as in the top-right switcher, then "Clear selection". S5-R2, S5-R3, S5-R4, S5-R5, S5-R6." (caption of "The native Location menu")

Design note (DR-02): the design shows with one location unticked and the menu still open, the ticked location is listed second ("Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" unticked above "Staging Lethbridge - 4310" ticked). Closed without a question: No conflict: PRD S5-R2 "the locations with the ticked ones first" is checked when the menu is opened again (S5-02, S5-03 close and reopen it); the picture shows the menu still open, where nothing moves. Native as on Sales By Customer.
